overview: 524 Lincoln Ave is a ten-unit apartment property in Northwest Pasadena consisting of an eight-unit 1925 building that was fully renovated in 2025 and two detached accessory dwelling units completed the same year. The original building totals 5,392 SF on a 10,945 SF PSR3-zoned lot.

Six units are occupied and four are vacant, including both new ADUs. Scheduled income in this analysis includes all four at their asking rents. Ownership acquired the property in December 2020, completed the renovation and ADU program in 2025, and operates it with third-party professional management.

The property fits private investors seeking turnkey Pasadena rental product: a fully renovated building with two new-construction ADUs, four units of immediate lease-up income, and room to move the occupied units to market on turnover.
properties.location_title: Northwest Pasadena, minutes from Old Pasadena and the Rose Bowl
location_narrative: The property sits on Lincoln Avenue in Northwest Pasadena, within roughly a mile of Old Pasadena, the Rose Bowl and the Foothill Freeway.
The surrounding blocks are a mix of small apartment buildings and single-family homes, and leased one-bedrooms in the immediate area run $2,100 to $2,300 per month.
Pasadena's employment base, school system and walkable core support durable occupancy for well-maintained smaller properties.
physical_narrative: The original building is a two-story wood-frame structure totaling 5,392 SF with four one-bedroom and four two-bedroom units, fully renovated in 2025 per ownership.
The two detached ADUs are new 2025 construction of 600 SF each; total building area of approximately 6,592 SF includes the ADU square footage.
One-bedroom units are approximately 650 SF and two-bedroom units approximately 698 SF per ownership.
market_narrative: Pasadena multifamily continues to trade actively in the 5 to 8 unit range, with six closed sales in the surrounding blocks since August 2025 spanning $217,000 to $300,000 per unit and 5.17% to 6.52% cap rates on in-place income.

Every one of those sales is unrenovated 1920s through 1960s product, so a buyer comparing this offering is choosing between deferred maintenance at a lower price per unit and a finished building at a higher one.
positioning_narrative: The property is positioned for private investors and 1031 buyers who want completed renovation work, new-construction income, and a manageable ten-unit operation.
rent_narrative: Leased one-bedrooms in the surrounding blocks run $2,100 to $2,300 per month and leased two-bedrooms run $2,300 to $2,495. The underwritten market rents of $2,250 and $2,450 sit inside both ranges.
The two-bedroom comparables carry larger floor plans than the subject's, so the two-bedroom conclusion is set below the top of the range rather than at it.
valuation_narrative: The recommended list price is $2,840,000, within a supported range of $2.75M to $2.95M. On the ten units with the four vacant units at asking rents, the price reflects a 6.50% current cap rate and 10.28 GRM, improving to a 6.76% cap rate at underwritten market rents on turnover. With occupied rents already within about 3% of underwritten market levels, the price is set on day-one yield rather than projected upside. Real estate taxes are underwritten at reassessment on the list price.

At $284,000 per unit the price sits in the upper half of the $217,000 to $300,000 per unit range set by the comparable sales, every one of which is unrenovated 1920s through 1960s product. The 2025 renovation, the two new-construction ADUs, and a 6.50% day-one yield at the top of the 5.17% to 6.52% band on older, un-upgraded buildings are what carry that position.
The lease-up of the four vacant units is the primary execution item; at asking rents they represent $112,800 of the $276,240 annual scheduled gross income.

strategy.title: Lead with the Completed Renovation
strategy.copy: Every comparable sale in the set is unrenovated 1920s through 1960s product. The completed 2025 renovation and the two new units are what separate this offering, and the campaign should open with them.

strategy.title: Show the Lease-Up as Upside
strategy.copy: Four units are vacant and ready to lease. Presented as immediate lease-up rather than as a vacancy problem, that is the clearest path a buyer has to grow income from day one.

strategy.title: Price Against Older Product
strategy.copy: Anchor the price conversation on the condition gap against the comparable sales, then let the day-one yield carry the rest.

disclosures: Rent roll and operating figures for the original eight units are transcribed from the July 31, 2026 rent roll and July 2026 cash flow statement prepared by Focus Property Services Inc. The two ADUs do not yet appear on the property management rent roll.
Units 101 and 102 and both ADUs are vacant; scheduled income includes all four at asking rents of $2,250 (one-bedroom) and $2,450 (ADU).

The property was originally constructed in 1925 and was fully renovated in 2025, when the two ADUs were completed, per ownership. Renovation scope, ADU permits, certificates of occupancy, and ADU square footage (600 SF each per ownership) should be independently verified.
Total building area of approximately 6,592 SF includes the ADU square footage; the original building is 5,392 SF per county records.

The property is subject to the City of Pasadena rent stabilization ordinance (Measure H). Annual increases on occupied units are limited by the ordinance; state law permits re-rent at market on vacancy. New-construction ADUs may be exempt from local rent caps under state law; verify applicability.

Comparable sale data is drawn from public records and industry databases and should be independently verified. The 1757 E Villa St sale is carried at the county-recorded price of $1,457,000 (grant deed 26-0505812); the seller trust carried a $1,000,000 loan, so that price reflects seller financing terms.
Interior and exterior photography of the renovated building is published by the property's own management company; additional exterior photography was taken by the listing team in August 2026.
This analysis is a broker opinion of value, not an appraisal. All figures should be independently verified during due diligence.

valuation_narrative: The recommended list price is $3,030,000, within a supported range of $2.95M to $3.15M. On the ten units with the four vacant units at asking rents, the price reflects a 6.02% current cap rate and 10.97 GRM, improving to a 6.26% cap rate at underwritten market rents on turnover. Real estate taxes are underwritten at reassessment on the list price.

At $303,000 per unit the price sits above the $217,000 to $300,000 per unit range set by the comparable sales, every one of which is unrenovated 1920s through 1960s product. The 2025 renovation, the two new-construction ADUs, and a 6.02% day-one yield against comparable sales trading between 5.17% and 6.52% on older, un-upgraded buildings are what carry that position.
The lease-up of the four vacant units is the primary execution item; at asking rents they represent $112,800 of the $276,240 annual scheduled gross income.

Price Against Older Product

Every comparable sale in the set is unrenovated 1920s through 1960s product. The completed 2025 renovation and the two new units are what separate this offering, and the campaign should open with them.
Four units are vacant and ready to lease. Presented as immediate lease-up rather than as a vacancy problem, that is the clearest path a buyer has to grow income from day one.
Anchor the price conversation on the condition gap against the comparable sales, then let the day-one yield carry the rest.
The proposed campaign combines direct buyer outreach, the Marcus & Millichap platform, and a dedicated digital presentation.
Ten units: eight fully renovated apartments plus two detached ADUs completed in 2025
Originally built 1925 and fully renovated in 2025 inside and out
Four one-bedroom, four two-bedroom, and two new-construction two-bedroom ADU floor plans
Four vacant units, including both new ADUs, ready for immediate lease-up at asking rents
Occupied rents average $2,270 per month with room to move to market on turnover
10,945 SF (0.25 acre) PSR3-zoned lot with on-site parking

524 Lincoln Ave is a ten-unit apartment property in Northwest Pasadena consisting of an eight-unit 1925 building that was fully renovated in 2025 and two detached accessory dwelling units completed the same year. The original building totals 5,392 SF on a 10,945 SF PSR3-zoned lot.

Six units are occupied and four are vacant, including both new ADUs. Scheduled income in this analysis includes all four at their asking rents. Ownership acquired the property in December 2020, completed the renovation and ADU program in 2025, and operates it with third-party professional management.

The property fits private investors seeking turnkey Pasadena rental product: a fully renovated building with two new-construction ADUs, four units of immediate lease-up income, and room to move the occupied units to market on turnover.
Northwest Pasadena, minutes from Old Pasadena and the Rose Bowl
The property sits on Lincoln Avenue in Northwest Pasadena, within roughly a mile of Old Pasadena, the Rose Bowl and the Foothill Freeway.
The surrounding blocks are a mix of small apartment buildings and single-family homes, and leased one-bedrooms in the immediate area run $2,100 to $2,300 per month.
Pasadena's employment base, school system and walkable core support durable occupancy for well-maintained smaller properties.
The original building is a two-story wood-frame structure totaling 5,392 SF with four one-bedroom and four two-bedroom units, fully renovated in 2025 per ownership.
The two detached ADUs are new 2025 construction of 600 SF each; total building area of approximately 6,592 SF includes the ADU square footage.
One-bedroom units are approximately 650 SF and two-bedroom units approximately 698 SF per ownership.
